items.title: WATCH: Brawl breaks out during Michigan, Michigan State NCAA hockey game
items.summary: Four game disqualifications and 126 minutes in penalties were handed out in the melee.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The rivalry between the University of Michigan and Michigan State University is one of the fiercest in all of college hockey. However, things got a little nastier than usual on Friday night. In the first of a home-and-home series between the No. 1 Wolverines and No. 9 Spartans, Michigan was running away with a 5-1 win at Yost Ice Arena. Then, just after the seven-minute mark of the third period, chaos ensued. It all started when Spartan defenseman and New York Rangers prospect Sean Barnhill laid a hit from behind on Wolverine forward Nick Moldenhauer, a Toronto Maple Leafs draft pick. That immediately sparked a kerfuffle between the players on the ice. It seemed that would be the end of it. However, Spartan captain Patrick Geary ( Buffalo Sabres ) got into it with several of the Wolverines near the Michigan bench, including goaltender Jack Ivankovic ( Nashville Predators ). That led to many players joining the fray who shouldn’t have. Barnhill and teammates Shane Vansaghi ( Philadelphia Flyers ) and Matthew Lahey (Maple Leafs) left the penalty box to get involved. Adam Valentini ( Utah Mammoth ) and Aidan Park ( Edmonton Oilers ) left the Michigan bench to join in on the action. After reviewing the video, no other Spartans left their bench to get involved. There were plenty of questionable actions by both sides during the fight, including Flyers prospect Jack Nesbitt punching Geary while he was lying on the ice. items.title: Line brawl breaks out between Michigan, Michigan State
items.body: There is no love lost between the University of Michigan and Michigan State hockey teams. A line brawl broke out on Friday night between the intra-state rivals — a rarity in college hockey, where the NCAA strictly prohibits fighting across all sports, including hockey. The melee started when Michigan State defenceman Sean Barnhill laid a hit from behind on Michigan forward and Toronto Maple Leafs prospect Nick Moldenhauer. Multiple fights ensued with members of the Michigan State penalty box skating out to join in on the fracas. In total, a combined 71 penalty minutes were handed out, including five major penalties and four disqualifications. Per the NCAA prohibition on fighting, a disqualification results in an automatic one-game suspension. Players facing the ban include Barnhill, Nick Sima, Drew Shock and Montreal Canadiens prospect Michael Hage. Time will tell if a rematch is in order or if cooler heads will prevail, as the two teams face each other again on Saturday night.

items.title: Huberdeau 'touched' by Flames support in long-awaited return to ice
items.summary: BROSSARD, Quebec -- Jonathan Huberdeau received the best possible show of affection for his return to hockey on Wednesday after having a left hip resurfacing operation in March.
items.body: Teammates cheer on forward in AHL rehab assignment in recovery from hip surgery BROSSARD, Quebec -- Jonathan Huberdeau received the best possible show of affection for his return to hockey on Wednesday after having a left hip resurfacing operation in March. In his first game with the Calgary Wranglers in the American Hockey League, Huberdeau played in front of several of his Calgary Flames colleagues, as well as under the watchful eye of Flames coach Ryan Huska. "It really warmed my heart. I was so touched to see my teammates there," said Huberdeau. "My little boy and my girlfriend were also there, watching me during warmups over by the boards, along with some other team dads. "The (Flames) had a travel day; they were coming back from San Jose. They weren't obligated to come to the arena; they could've used the day to rest up. But they wanted to come cheer me on. I'm there for my teammates, but I also realize that they're there for me. They've still got my back, they're rooting for me to get healthy again. I didn't think there would be so many of them." Flames captain Mikael Backlund , forwards Ryan Strome , Morgan Frost , Matt Coronato and Joel Farabee , and defensemen Joel Hanley and Zayne Parekh all watched from the stands at Scotiabank Saddledome as Huberdeau registered three assists, leading the Wranglers to a 4-3 victory against Coachella Valley on Wednesday. "’Jo’ is a guy who's highly respected by the organization and by his teammates," said Wranglers coach Brett Sutter. "We saw proof of that in our game, since I think about half the Flames players flew in to come watch him. That shows how much guys in the organization care about him. He's a big part of things here." items.body: Facebook icon Twitter icon Reddit icon Copy icon Link Copied Add RMNB as a preferred source on Google ARLINGTON, VA — For the first time since Logan Thompson arrived in DC, the Washington Capitals have a goaltending problem. Thompson, arguably the team’s best player over the last two seasons, has looked little like his former self this month. In seven starts since November 1, Thompson has allowed an average of 3.4 goals per game for just a .841 save percentage, giving up goals on opponents’ first shot of the game three times in under three weeks. Head coach Spencer Carbery pulled Thompson just once in his first 110 games for Washington; he’s now done so twice in six games. As the Capitals look to snap Thompson out of his funk, they have two options. They could opt to keep playing Thompson, getting him back on the horse as soon as possible. Or they could start Charlie Lindgren , giving Thompson time to reset before going back in the net. “We haven’t made a decision on what’s going to go on for tomorrow night,” Carbery said. “There’s some times where you just want to let a guy play through some struggles, and then there’s sometimes where you’d like him to take a step back. “Both can be utilized and both are appropriate at given times, and that’s just up to (goaltending coach) Scotty Murray, Logan, myself, and making the best decision possible.” The pros and cons of each approach go beyond a single game. items.body: CALGARY — There aren't many equipment managers who get to celebrate a highlight-reel assist, get a shoutout on Sportsnet and have an NHL defenceman searching for a fine bottle of wine for them. Ben Dumaine managed all three Thursday night, thanks to a quick reaction that helped Simon Nemec turn a broken stick into a beautiful goal. After going viral with the stick fix, the 37-year-old Flames assistant equipment manager arrived at the Saddledome Friday morning a bashful celebrity of sorts. “Joel Hanley came up to me and said, ‘You’ve got more assists than I do this year,'" chuckled the popular dressing room assistant. It's a pretty unique accomplishment for a guy whose usual highlights involve skate sharpeners, laundry and equipment bags. Nemec had his stick slashed in half in his own zone Thursday against Minnesota, and while approaching the bench with speed, he contemplated a change when he spotted Dumaine holding out his backup. He grabbed it on the fly, kept going up ice and turned a two-on-one into a three-on-one. Morgan Frost delivered a slick pass, and Nemec one-timed it home. “I might get him a bottle of wine or something,” said Nemec, dubbing it a “pretty sick goal.” “I mean, he was a big part of that. He had the stick ready for me and I had pretty good speed, so I used that and it went in.” Here's the best part: Dumaine didn't see the stick break, never saw the goal, and had no idea what an integral role he played in it. Detroit offered no specifics about the injury, only that Johansson would miss several weeks and that he suffered the ailment against the Calgary Flames on October 24th. Before the injury, the third-year blue liner had appeared in 11 contests. He was responsible on the ice, registering one assist with a +1 rating, while averaging 15:41 of ice time per game. Because they have only 22 players on the active roster, the Red Wings don’t necessarily need to make an additional roster move to activate Johansson. Still, when they officially activate him, they’ll have eight defensemen on the NHL roster. Detroit could certainly use all the help they can get, but even eight defensemen is one too many. The key factor in demoting an additional blueliner is William Wallinder ’s status. items.body: Photo: David Dwork Photo: David Dwork Prospect Watch: How Panthers' Ignatavicius' Lithuanian Background Molded A Unique Path To The NHL Ryan Kennedy Partner Nov 20, 2026 8:47 PM Published Nov 20, 2026 8:47 PM In the sports world, Lithuania is known for basketball. But Simas Ignatavicius chose ice over hardwood, and the Florida Panthers prospect is proving that was the right decision. We love a good backstory in hockey and Simas Ignatavicius brings it. Born in Memphis, Tennessee, to a pro basketball player from Lithuania, he moved back home as a toddler where he caught the hockey bug instead of hoops. "Obviously my dad wanted me to play basketball, but my mom said to let me try other sports first," he said. "In Lithuania we really only have three or four ice rinks, all the rest are in malls. I was having pizza with my dad one day and there was a practice going on. More Videos "I saw someone on skates, playing with the puck, for the first time in my life. And I wanted to try it. So thanks, pizza." Ignatavicius eventually got so good that a decision had to be made about his future. Of course, he was only 12 at the time, so it was daunting to consider moving to Switzerland without his parents. "I had a talk with my dad before signing the contract," he said. "My dad looked me straight in the eye and asked 'Are you sure you want to do this? Because it takes a lot of sacrifice, money-wise.' I said 'yes' right away, I didn't hesitate. That's when he knew I was serious. He and my mom gave me the green light after that." The youngster lived with a billet family, but it was still hard to be away from his family. items.title: Leafs’ Jim Hiller says job security ‘Not something I think about too much’ following eighth-straight loss
items.summary: Toronto sits in last place in the Atlantic Division with 19 points through 24 games.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images As the Toronto Maple Leafs continue to plummet down the standings, with Thursday’s 4-3 shootout loss to the Los Angeles Kings marking their eighth defeat in a row, it’s hard not to wonder whether head coach Jim Hiller could be relieved of his duties sooner rather than later. One person, however, that apparently isn’t worried about the coach’s job security, is Hiller himself. After Toronto’s general manager John Chayka expressed his belief in Hiller on Monday, Hiller spoke to reporters on Friday and addressed the rumors that his job could be in jeopardy. “Not something I think about too much,” Hiller said. “I appreciate that John did that. My job is to get the team to win games. We haven’t won enough, so I get them ready to win tomorrow.” Among other criticisms, Hiller’s handling of winger Gavin McKenna, the first-overall pick in the 2026 NHL Entry Draft, has come under scrutiny. The 18-year-old rookie did not receive a shift during Thursday’s 3-on-3 overtime period against the Kings. Hiller discussed his rationale behind keeping McKenna on the bench for overtime. “I think when we have some time where we’ll do some 3-on-3,” Hiller said. “We haven’t had a lot of practice time this year in getting preparation for the season. It’s a short season. But we’re going to do that. And then during that time, he’s going to get some of those reps.” The Leafs hired Hiller as their head coach in June following the firing of Craig Berube, who spent the previous two seasons as the bench boss in Toronto. Hiller had been the head coach of the Kings from February of 2024 until March of 2026. With 19 points through 24 games, the Leafs sit in last place in the Atlantic Division , and will host the Columbus Blue Jackets on Saturday.

items.title: Vanguards name Erin Ambrose team’s first captain
items.summary: Hayley Scamurra and rookie Tessa Janecke have been named alternate captains for Vegas’ inaugural season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources One of the game’s most respected players has earned a new title with one of the PWHL’s newest franchises. On Friday, the Vegas Vanguards announced that the team has named defender Erin Ambrose the first captain in franchise history. Forwards Hayley Scamurra and Tessa Janecke have been named alternates for the expansion team’s inaugural season. Ambrose was one of the foundational signings for the franchise in Sin City. She brings immediate legitimacy to the team and stability on the blue line. The Canadian National Team mainstay spent the first three seasons of the PWHL with the Montreal Victoire, helping the team win its first Walter Cup this past spring. This isn’t the first time Ambrose is in a leadership role in the PWHL. During her time with the Victoire, she was an alternate captain, supporting Marie-Philip Poulin . The Keswick, Ont. native will be seeking her first goal since the league’s first season with her new team, as Ambrose posted just six assists in 21 regular-season games last year. In 73 regular-season contests in her PWHL career, Ambrose has scored four goals and 37 points, with another five points in 16 playoff contests. Scamurra comes to Vegas with Ambrose from Montreal. She’s coming off the best season of her tenure in the league, scoring eight goals and 16 points during the regular season, adding another four points in the postseason. Janecke is thrust into the spotlight with the Vanguards. She was the team’s first-ever draft pick, taken third overall in the 2026 PWHL Draft in June. She enters the PWHL after a sensational career at Penn State, where she was a top-three finalist for the Patty Kazmaier Award in her senior season. The Vanguards begin their first season on Dec. 6, hosting the fellow expansion Detroit Clutch.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: James Guillory-Imagn Images The Winnipeg Jets have placed goaltender Clay Stevenson on waivers for the purpose of assignment to the AHL’s Manitoba Moose, PuckPedia reported Friday afternoon. Stevenson, 27, appeared in five games with the Jets to start the 2026-27 season after being claimed off waivers from the Washington Capitals on Sept. 28. The 6’4″ goaltender posted a 1-3-0 record with an .870 save percentage in his five appearances with the club. The Jets had been running with three goaltenders on their active roster since acquiring Nico Daws from the New Jersey Devils in the Connor Hellebuyck trade. Friday’s news would seem to indicate that the Jets have decided to go with Daws and Stuart Skinner between the pipes going forward. As PuckPedia noted on Friday, the Capitals would be able to assign Stevenson directly to the AHL’s Hershey Bears if they are the only team to submit a claim for the goaltender. An undrafted player, Stevenson spent three seasons with the BCHL’s Coquitlam Express between 2017 and 2020 before heading to Dartmouth College, where he played the 2021-22 campaign. The Capitals opted to sign Stevenson to an entry-level contract as an NCAA free agent on Mar. 28, 2022. The Drayton Valley, Alta. product spent most of the 2022-23 season with the ECHL’s South Carolina Stingrays before being promoted to the Bears, with whom he won the Calder Cup in 2024. Stevenson made his NHL debut with the Capitals in the 2024-25 season and appeared in four more games with the club the following year. The Capitals chose to waive Stevenson on the eve of the 2026-27 regular season, leading the Jets — grappling with Hellebuyck’s absence — to submit a claim. items.title: Leafs meet with golfer Rory McIlroy, sports psychologist Dr. Bob Rotella during eight-game losing streak
items.summary: McIlroy and Rotella spent two hours talking to the team on Friday morning.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources In the midst of an abysmal eight-game losing streak that is threatening to effectively sink their season, the Toronto Maple Leafs are seeking outside advice on how to snap out of their funk. On The Fan Hockey Show, Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman revealed that Leafs captain Auston Matthews and renowned golfer Rory McIlroy spoke for an hour following Thursday’s 4-3 shootout loss to the Los Angeles Kings . On Friday morning, McIlroy and sports psychologist Dr. Bob Rotella spent two hours talking to the team as a whole. McIlroy, 37, is one of the greatest men’s golfers of all time, having won six major championships along with several other individual honors. Perhaps most relevant to the Leafs current circumstances, he’s also dealt with adversity during his career, famously collapsing in the final round of the 2011 Masters and going a decade without a major championship after winning The Open Championship in 2014. Rotella has worked as McIlroy’s sports psychologist for the majority of his career. He is the best-selling author of several books, including 2016’s How Champions Think: In Sports and Life and other more golf-specific titles. In a recent Heavy.com article , McIlroy explained how Rotella helps his mental state while performing. “He does such a great job of simplifying things and breaking things down into very bite-sized pieces that you can take with you onto the golf course, and little mantras and little sayings,” he said. While issues with the Leafs’ roster construction, which have been exacerbated by injuries, have stood out during this losing streak, it’s hard to deny that there’s likely also a mental component in play. The Mammoth made several big moves dating back to last season, acquiring MacKenzie Weegar , Anders Lee , Vincent Trocheck , and young goaltender Sebastian Cossa , whom they brought in from the Detroit Red Wings in a summer trade. The acquisition of Cossa left the Mammoth with a tandem of Cossa and Karel Vejmelka , which the team felt comfortable with, and for good reason. However, a quarter of the way through the season, the Mammoth have to be concerned about the goaltending they’ve received. Overall, the team has played well, controlling roughly 57% of the expected goals at five-on-five, which ranks second in the NHL. They’re also allowing 2.15 expected goals against per 60 minutes, which is solid. Despite these underlying numbers, the team has been outscored at five-on-five so far this season, largely due to inconsistent goaltending. Vejmelka has been a shell of himself this year compared with his work from just a season ago. items.title: Kings’ Adrian Kempe fined for high-sticking Leafs’ Dakota Joshua
items.summary: Kempe was handed a double-minor for penalty for the incident, but later came back to score the shootout winner.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images A talented player is paying up for actions in The Six. On Friday, the NHL Department of Player Safety announced that Los Angeles Kings forward Adrian Kempe has been fined $3,500 for high-sticking Toronto Maple Leafs forward Dakota Joshua. The incident came a little past the halfway mark of the first period of Thursday night’s game between the two teams. In the Kings’ zone, Joshua was attempting to drive toward the front of the net. Kempe, trying to run interference, caught Joshua with a cross-check to the face, leaving the latter a little bloodied. Kempe was given a double-minor penalty for high-sticking on the play. The Leafs ended up scoring on the extended power play, with captain Auston Matthews scoring his 13th goal of the season. However, Kempe and the Kings got the last laugh. Los Angeles rallied from a 3-0 deficit, with Kempe picking up an assist along the way, to force overtime. The 30-year-old proceeded to score the lone goal in the shootout, giving the Kings a hard-fought 4-3 win. This isn’t the first time Kempe has faced supplemental discipline in his NHL career. In January 2025, the Swedish winger was fined $5,000 for slew-footing Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid. Kempe has never been suspended by the NHL DoPS. The money from the fine goes to the Players’ Emergency Assistance Fund. In 19 games this season, Kempe ranks second on the Kings in goals (6), tied for second in points (14) and fourth in assists (8). Thursday’s win was welcome for the Kings, as the team has struggled for much of the first quarter of the 2026-27 season. items.title: Red Wings’ Albert Johansson to return after 11-game absence
items.summary: The Swedish blueliner has been out since late October due to an undisclosed ailment.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Some positive news in Hockeytown heading into the weekend. When speaking to the media on Friday, Detroit Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan revealed that defenseman Albert Johansson will be back in the lineup on Saturday night, when the Red Wings play host to the New York Islanders . Johansson has been out of action since Oct. 24, when he reportedly suffered an injury. However, it has yet to be disclosed what exactly knocked the Swedish blueliner out of action. He has since missed the past 11 games, which has seen Detroit struggle to keep up in the Eastern Conference Wild Card race. The Red Wings have gone 4-7-0 with Johansson out of the lineup, having lost five of their past six contests. Johansson has done little to contribute to Detroit’s offense this season, though he has spent most of the first quarter of the 2026-27 campaign in the top four. In 11 contests, the 25-year-old has yet to find the back of the net, with just one assist coming in a 5-2 win over the Vancouver Canucks on Oct. 22. He has a plus/minus of +1, while averaging 15:41 of ice time per game. This is Johansson’s third full season in the NHL. He entered the year after appearing in all 82 games in 2025-26, posting three goals and a career-best 11 points. In 154 games with the Wings, he has totaled six goals and 15 assists for 21 points. Johansson is in the second season of his two-year contract extension, which he signed in June 2025. The deal carries an AAV of $1.125 million, and he is set to be a restricted free agent on July 1. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On Friday, the Berner Jura-Seeland Regional Prosecutor’s Office in Switzerland announced that it has opened an investigation regarding an incident involving former NHL forward Daniel Carr, who was involved in a fight last month. The incident in question came on Oct. 16 during a game between Carr’s HC Ajoie and EHC Biel. Carr was ejected from the game for his actions and was subsequently suspended for five games by the National League. Biel appealed the decision, resulting in the suspension being increased to seven games. items.summary: The backbone, fortitude and discipline that allowed the Canucks to build a two-game win streak were wholly absent in Seattle.
items.body: SEATTLE — Winning streaks. So hard to build, so easy to blow. After waiting 23 games to construct their first two-game winning streak of the National Hockey League season, the Vancouver Canucks never gave themselves a chance here Thursday to count to three. Actually, goalie Leevi Merilainen gave the Canucks a chance, but he was about the only one. Teammates didn’t respond or rally around his brilliant performance through 28 minutes and eventually lost 5-1 to the Seattle Kraken. The backbone, fortitude and discipline that allowed the Canucks to respond to difficult stretches or untimely goals-against in their surprising wins this week against the Vegas Golden Knights and Utah Mammoth were wholly absent in Seattle. After getting outshot 24-5 in the opening period, the Canucks surrendered another nine shots in the first nine minutes of the second. The Kraken scored twice in 54 seconds, starting at the eight-minute mark, to pull ahead 3-1. And given the avalanche of shots and Kraken skaters bombarding Merilainen’s net, the Canucks never looked capable of coming back from two goals down. The Canucks have false-started in a pile of games this season, and posted absolute duds in a few. But even for a last-place team, their reversal in form from Las Vegas and Salt Lake City was surprising. “A little bit,” Canucks coach Manny Malhotra conceded. “Just in terms of how off we were and how badly we got outshot. (I was) expecting a better response. I think the guys had a much clearer understanding coming into tonight that we earned what we got in our previous two games just by the work ethic — the winning of puck battles, establishing a forecheck, those types of things. With the assist, Stone gets the 418th point of his Golden Knights career, and puts him atop the franchise’s all-time scoring records. He surpasses Jonathan Marchessault, who had established the previous record of 417 points ever since the end of the 2023-24 season, his final season in Vegas before departing in free agency and signing with the Nashville Predators . This season, Stone has continued his established consistency on the scoresheet since joining the Golden Knights, as he has 11 goals and 11 assists for 22 points in 24 games . Jake DeBrusk scored for the Canucks, who had won two in a row, while Leevi Merilainen made 38 saves. Catton scored a goal in each period starting with a power-play goal in the first. DeBrusk countered with a power-play goal to make it 1-1 after the first period. Catton and Beniers scored 54 seconds apart in the second to make it 3-1 Seattle after two periods, and Catton capped the hat trick with an empty-netter with 43 seconds remaining. Ovechkin’s 763rd assist to surpass Nicklas Backstrom ’s Capitals record was mostly a footnote following a 6-3 loss to the Buffalo Sabres at Capital One Arena on Thursday. It was the fourth consecutive loss for Washington, which allowed at least five goals in each of the defeats, and fell to a disappointing 10-10-0 through its first 20 games. “We just have to keep fighting,” Ovechkin said. “Sometimes things don't go your way, but we just have to keep fighting and stay with it.” Ovechkin has been fighting it all season. The NHL’s all-time leader with 930 goals has scored just one through his first 20 games and was held without one for the 15th straight game Thursday. That’s the longest goal drought of his 22-season NHL career, exceeding one of 14 games from Nov. 22-Dec. 20, 2023. The 41-year-old left wing has six points (one goal, five assists) this season, including just two (both assists) in his past 12 games. “Chances are there,” Ovechkin said. “It’s just sometimes you hold the stick too tight. The 22-year-old left winger was the first NHL player with a goal in 10 consecutive games since Teemu Selanne set the Anaheim record with an 11-game run in 1997. Gauthier had four hat tricks during the streak, including Tuesday night in an 8-6 defeat at St. Louis. items.summary: For now, the Maple Leafs will have to settle for a single point gained, a small step forward even if it comes amid continued stumbles.
items.body: TORONTO — For a moment Thursday night, it seemed the Toronto Maple Leafs had found some progress. Some momentum, some life. For the first time in this stretch of what's now eight straight games without a win, the Maple Leafs made their way to the locker room after 20 minutes with a two-goal lead and their opponents held off the board. A much-needed power-play marker from Auston Matthews had drawn first blood against the visiting Los Angeles Kings. The captain then set up another, dancing through the offensive zone and finding John Tavares. Fourth-liners Brandon Duhaime and Teddy Blueger dropped the gloves with a couple of Kings before the period was through, sending Toronto to the room with a pair of goals and a pair of fights. Two minutes into the second period, the home side kept it rolling. items.title: Lane Hutson leads Canadiens to gutsiest win of season
items.summary: The Hurricanes tried to push them. But Lane Hutson and the Canadiens didn’t just get up and push back, they pushed the Hurricanes over in a way they haven’t been able to in recent memory.
items.body: This was Lane Hutson as we’ve never seen him before — doubled over, gasping for the air that had been knocked out of him by the type of hit he’s so rarely been on the receiving end of since he jitterbugged his way into the NHL at the end of the 2023-24 season. Hutson was uncharacteristically lackadaisical, atypically unaware of Shayne Gostisbehere’s presence. He never saw it coming. But it was Gostisbehere and the Carolina Hurricanes who, in the end, were on the end of an unforeseen outcome. Because Hutson bounced back up from that second-period hit that left him winded and eventually took everyone’s breath away. First with a stunner of a tying goal late in the third period. And then with the winner that made it 2-1 Montreal Canadiens in overtime to cap their gutsiest performance of the season. “Everyone stepped up,” Hutson told reporters at Lenovo Center. That was right after Canadiens coach Martin St. Louis referred to it as a win that made them “better as a team.” It’s exactly what we were thinking with each passing minute of the game, as the Canadiens finally bore their teeth against this hungry pack of wolves. Oh sure, they beat the Hurricanes three times last regular season and once more at the start of the Eastern Conference Final last spring. But none of those games looked like this one, with the Canadiens pinching all the pressure points the Hurricanes typically have a firm grasp of. That they did it less than 24 hours after registering a bounce-back win against the red-hot Devils in New Jersey, that they did it missing several key players, and that they did it against a Hurricanes team that’s still sitting with the NHL’s best points percentage (.795) despite the loss, said everything about how much their character has grown since that lopsided playoff series.

The Minnesota Wild had to be concerned a bit with their goaltending entering this season, considering one half of their outstanding tandem, Filip Gustavsson , was going to miss some time recovering from hip surgery in May. That would put the burden on Jesper Wallstedt , who started 10 of the Wild's 11 games in the 2026 Stanley Cup Playoffs after starting consecutive games only twice during the regular season. So, could Wallstedt, who turned 24 on Nov. 14, carry the load by himself? Judging by the first quarter of the season, he's answered any questions. Wallstedt has started 20 of Minnesota’s first 23 games and is 16-2-3 with a 1.95 goals-against average and .926 save percentage. His play has helped the Wild (17-3-4) take a nine-point lead atop the competitive Central Division. He's allowed two goals or fewer 15 times, and his .934 save percentage at even strength ranks third among NHL goalies who have started at least 10 games (Linus Ullmark, Ottawa Senators, .964; Daniil Tarasov, Detroit Red Wings, .941). items.body: The Minnesota Wild picked up a 4-1 win over the Calgary Flames on Thursday, but it may have come at a price. It was Hockey Fights Cancer night in Pittsburgh and Florio used her airtime to share her personal story. At 15 years old she was diagnosed with a brain tumor. Florio went on to thank everyone who supported her and her doctors at Duke Children's Hospital, sharing a picture with her pediatric neurosurgeon, Dr. Fuchs. "I can now sit here today and say I'm here, I'm healthy, I beat it and I am so, so thankful for that," she said. To open up the spot star defenseman Cale Makar has landed on injured reserve, reported by Ryan O’Hara of The Hockey News . A headline which always captures attention, Makar’s status is not surprising as five days ago it was revealed that he’d miss at least two weeks with his lower-body injury. Without the two-time Norris winner the Avs have leaned on impressive undrafted right-hander Sam Malinski . Beckman, 25, will have the opportunity to play in his first NHL contest since April 2024 as a member of the Wild. Drafted by Minnesota in the third round seven years ago, the winger broke the 100-point mark in his last full junior season as a Spokane Chief, generating some hype with his high end shot and making a quick Wild debut at age 20. Suiting up for 22 more games over the years with three assists, at this point he has made most of his impact in the AHL. Proving himself as a reliable scorer for the Iowa Wild with defensive shortcomings, not uncommon for non-prospects who light up the AHL, the Saskatoon native Beckman made stops with the Utica Comets and Bridgeport Islanders. He put together a 30-goal campaign last season for the New York farm club prior to catching on as part of the Avalanche organization. Usually they take about two weeks,” Falkenberg said. “Pepsi supplied the boxes and they all come in flat, so I have to fold them all into shape and then assemble them into pieces and transport them down.” Falkenberg has worked for Save-On-Foods in Kelowna, B.C., for the past 28 years and has been building displays for stores in the province for the past 10 years. Adam Proteau Partner Nov 20, 2026 12:11 AM Published Nov 20, 2026 12:11 AM Updated Nov 20, 2026 12:45 AM New NHL coaches are often the opposite of the bench bosses they've replaced, but has Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller really been different, or in any way better, than Craig Berube? As is often the case when NHL teams change coaches, the organization's choice for a new coach is someone with a significantly different philosophy than that of their predecessor. A team that failed with a coach who was more rigid or autocratic in their approach almost always ends up replaces him with a more player-friendly bench boss — and vice versa. So, when the Toronto Maple Leafs fired coach Craig Berube at the end of last season and replaced him with Jim Hiller, the idea was that Hiller would succeed at turning Toronto into a better defensive team than the one Berube tried to mold to fit his approach. Both go about their business in different ways, but has Hiller actually succeeded where Berube couldn't? items.body: Register Login Avalanche’s Gabriel Landeskog, Parker Kelly Fined By Brennan McClain | at November 19, 2026 5:00 pm The NHL’s Department of Player Safety has issued two separate fines from last night’s contest between the Colorado Avalanche and the Utah Mammoth. First, the DoPS fined Avalanche captain Gabriel Landeskog $5,000 (the maximum allowable) for cross-checking Mammoth forward Logan Cooley . The DoPS also fined Avalanche forward Parker Kelly $3,500 for high-sticking Mammoth forward Michael Carcone . There was an immediate expectation that Landeskog would face supplemental discipline. Early in the contest, Cooley attempted to hit Landeskog, and he ended up rolling over his back. Cooley attempted to stand up, but Landeskog repeatedly cross-checked him, even while he was on the ice, until he was eventually pulled off. The referees assessed Landeskog a double-minor for the incident. This isn’t the first time Landeskog has had a run-in with the Department of Player Safety. The former second-overall pick has been suspended four different times throughout his 13-year career, for 11 games total. Today’s discipline is his second career fine. The last time he was fined was during the 2014-15 season for punching the Minnesota Wild’s former captain, Mikko Koivu . Meanwhile, this is Kelly’s first time being fined. Still, like Landeskog, he’s faced discipline from the Department of Player Safety before. Toward the end of the 2023-24 campaign, Kelly received a two-game suspension for an illegal check to the head against Los Angeles Kings defenseman Andreas Englund . Landeskog would probably rather pay the fine than take the beating Jack McBain put on him last night. That was an a** wuppin!

items.summary: Filip Gustavsson went 28-15-6 with a .904 SV% and four shutouts in 50 games with the Minnesota Wild in 2025-26.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources The Minnesota Wild announced Thursday that goaltender Filip Gustavsson has been assigned to their AHL affiliate on a conditioning stint. He is expected to start for the Iowa Wild this Saturday against the San Diego Gulls. Gustavsson, 28, underwent hip surgery in the summer and started the season on injured reserve . In 2025-26, he went 28-15-6 with a .904 save percentage (SV%) and a 1.4 goals saved above expected (GSAx) with four shutouts in 50 games. This season will be the first in a five-year, $34-million contract extension that Gustavsson signed in October 2025. He will carry a cap hit of $6.8 million through the 2030-31 campaign. In six NHL seasons, the Skelleftea, Sweden, native is 111-74-26 with a .911 SV% and a 2.67 goals against average (GAA) in 219 appearances with the Wild and Ottawa Senators . He also has a 4-7 record with a .911 SV% and 2.67 GAA in 12 career Stanley Cup Playoff games. Gustavsson was taken in the second round of the 2016 NHL Entry Draft by the Pittsburgh Penguins . He spent two more seasons developing in Sweden’s top professional hockey league with Lulea HF before he moved to North America. In 2018, Gustavsson was traded to the Senators, along with Ian Cole, a first-round pick and a third-round pick in exchange for Derick Brassard. He spent parts of five seasons with their AHL affiliate, the Belleville Senators, where he posted a 45-39-8 record with an .898 SV% and 3.06 GAA in 95 appearances.

items.title: Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness set to return from health issue
items.body: Columbus Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness is set to resume his post behind the bench after missing three games with an undisclosed health issue. The 71-year-old informed the team of his return for their game against the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday before its road practice the day before. “We’ve missed a week,” Bowness told The Athletic. “That’s a long time, so I’m thrilled to be back. “It’s weird watching the games. It’s a little different. You’d rather be here with the guys. You want to be in the fight. That’s the biggest thing. It’s good to be back in the fight with these guys.” The Blue Jackets lost all three games in Bowness's absence. He stayed in Columbus on Monday to undergo various medical tests when the team first departed on its current four-game road trip. First-year assistant Don Granato took over the team while Bowness was away.

items.title: Report: Simon Edvinsson passed on multiple offer sheets to force exit from Red Wings
items.summary: Edvinsson must sign by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 to be eligible to play in the NHL this season.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images The situation between the Detroit Red Wings and defenseman Simon Edvinsson keeps getting uglier. Edvinsson, 23, is currently a restricted free agent, having not yet signed an extension with the Red Wings following the completion of his three-year, entry-level deal last season. He must sign a deal by 5 p.m. ET on December 1 in order to be eligible to play in the NHL this season. According to Sportsnet’s Frank Seravalli, Edvinsson has turned down offer sheets from multiple teams in order to deny Detroit the opportunity to match, putting pressure on the Red Wings to simply trade him before the December 1 deadline. “He’d love to be signed and playing,” a source told Seravalli. “But he no longer wants to play in Detroit and that would be the risk with an offer sheet.” Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff mentioned earlier this season that he has “zero interest” in trading Edvinsson. Horcoff may be forced to change his tune, or else risk losing Edvinsson for the season if nothing gets done ahead of the December 1 deadline. Detroit would still retain Edvinsson’s rights in that case, but would presumably receive less appealing trade offers for a player that could no longer play this season. Seravalli also pointed out that there is a daily cap penalty for the first year of a contract given to a restricted free agent after the start of the regular season, meaning the cap hit for this season on any deal Edvinsson may ultimately sign gets higher with each day he remains unsigned. Selected sixth overall by the Red Wings in the 2021 NHL Entry Draft, Edvinsson had nine goals and 16 assists for 25 points in 72 games with Detroit last season, while averaging just under 22 and half minutes of ice time.

items.title: Avalanche’s Landeskog, Kelly fined for incidents with Mammoth
items.body: The dust may have settled after a tense night in Utah, but not without a cost. Colorado Avalanche forwards Gabriel Landeskog and Parker Kelly were each fined by the NHL's department of player safety on Thursday for incidents that occurred in a loss to the Mammoth on Wednesday. Landeskog was fined $5,000 by the league for cross-checking Utah's Logan Cooley. The incident occurred late in the first period, after Cooley had skated into Landeskog while he was down on the ice, prompting the Avs captain to retaliate and strike the Mammoth forward from behind with multiple cross-checks. Upon review, Landeskog was assessed a double-minor on the play. Kelly was fined $3,500 for high-sticking Utah's Michael Carcone. Those were just some of the edgy moments between the Central Division rivals, in a game that included multiple big hits and fights — Landeskog squared up with Jack McBain, as did Alex Gagne and Liam O'Brien .

items.title: Avalanche’s Landeskog, Kelly fined following game against Mammoth
items.summary: The Avalanche fell 4-1 to the Mammoth at Delta Center in Salt Lake City on Wednesday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Rob Gray-Imagn Images The NHL’s Department of Player Safety has fined Colorado Avalanche forwards Gabriel Landeskog and Parker Kelly in response to stick infractions they committed during Wednesday’s game against the Utah Mammoth . Landeskog, 33, was fined $5,000 — the maximum allowable under the terms of the Collective Bargaining Agreement — for repeatedly cross-checking Utah’s Logan Cooley in the first period. The Avalanche captain was assessed two minor penalties for cross-checking on the play, with Utah’s Vincent Trocheck scoring the eventual game-winning goal on the ensuing power play. Kelly, 27, was fined $3,500 for high-sticking Mammoth forward Michael Carcone in the second period. The third-year Avalanche forward received a two-minute penalty on the play; he subsequently scored Colorado’s only goal of the game in the third period. The Mammoth won Wednesday’s game at the Delta Center by a 4-1 final score, with Liam O’Brien, Dmitri Simashev, and Kevin Stenlund joining Trocheck in finding the back of the net. Utah goaltender Sebastian Cossa stopped 30 of 31 Avalanche shots in the victory. Utah and Colorado combined for 42 minutes in penalties in the game, with Landeskog leading the way for either team with nine. The veteran winger dropped the gloves in the second period with Mammoth forward Jack McBain, who won the bout in decisive fashion . Landeskog is currently tied for eighth on the Avalanche with 13 points (eight goals, five assists) through 22 games this season, while Kelly sits just behind with 10 points (five goals, five assists).
